To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
‘the reduced basis method can be used to efficiently compute and a posteriori certify the accuracy of the outputs of interest of parabolic problems’.

the reduced-basis approach is a powerful method to solve efficiently and accurately parameter-dependent parabolic partial differential equations, and to compute ‘relevant’ output of interest with a ‘posteriori’ error estimation procedure that validates the accuracy of the predictions.
we can efficiently compute and certify the accuracy of output predictions of parameterized parabolic partial differential equations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a ‘reduced-order’ computational framework for ‘parameter-dependent’ parabolic problems, and its application to problems arising in the context of uncertainty quantification.
the construction and analysis of a ‘time-dependent’ reduced-basis method for parameterized parabolic problems, which is computationally efficient, accurate and reliable.
the development of reduced basis output bound methods for parameterized parabolic problems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we have developed a reduced-basis method for parabolic problems that is both efficient in terms of computational cost, and accurate in terms of output prediction, and that can be validated by an ‘a posteriori’ error estimator.
the reduced-basis output-bound method is a powerful tool for the solution and analysis of parabolic problems, and that it is an efficient and reliable alternative to POD.

we are able to construct reduced-basis approximations and output bounds that are ‘efficient’ (in the sense that the computational complexity scales linearly with the dimension of the parameter space), ‘accurate’ (in the reduced-basis sense), ‘reliable’ (in the output bound sense) and ‘robust’ (in the time discretization sense).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have extended POD methods to the time domain.

the reduced-basis procedure provides an efficient, yet accurate approximation to the solution, whereas the error estimation procedure provides an efficient validation tool to ensure the accuracy of the reduced-basis solution.
we develop an output bound reduced-basis method for parameterized parabolic problems, which is efficient, reliable, and computationally cheap.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, for a given number of snapshots, the error in the reduced-basis approximation is of the same order as the POD error, and that the reduced-basis error bound is of the same quality as the POD error bound.
the reduced-basis approach, combined with a POD-like procedure, provides an effective framework for the analysis, approximation, and error control of parabolic problems.
reduced-basis output-bound methods provide an effective way to efficiently compute accurate approximations of outputs of interest and ‘validate’ their accuracy.
